**APPENDIX B**

**INFORMED CONSENT FORM**

**Dear Participant**:

You are invited to participate in a research study conducted by Bachelor of Science in Information Technology students of Lorma Colleges. Before deciding whether to participate, please read the information below. You may ask the researchers to clarify anything you do not understand.

**Purpose of the Study**

The study aims to assess the financial management practices, budgeting challenges, and expense-tracking behaviors of parents and young professionals; design and develop the SmartSpend mobile application; and evaluate the application's usability using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and user feedback.

**Who May Participate**

The study focuses on parents aged 35–55 who serve as household financial managers and young professionals aged 21–35 who independently manage their income and expenses. Participation in the SUS evaluation is intended for eligible adult participants who have tried the SmartSpend application.

**Study Procedures**

Depending on the stage of the study, you may be invited to: (1) answer the financial-management survey; and/or (2) try the SmartSpend application through a demonstration or Demo Mode and complete the SUS questionnaire and optional feedback questions. The SUS questionnaire should be completed only after you have had an opportunity to use or explore the application.

**Voluntary Participation and Withdrawal**

Your participation is voluntary. You may decline to answer any question that you are not comfortable answering and may stop participating at any time without penalty or loss of any benefit to which you are otherwise entitled.

**Possible Risks and Benefits**

No significant risks are anticipated. Some questions concern personal or household financial practices, and you may skip a question if you do not wish to answer it. You may not receive a direct personal benefit; however, your responses may help the researchers improve the SmartSpend application and contribute to the study.

**Confidentiality and Data Handling**

The researchers will use the information collected for academic purposes. Survey and evaluation results will be summarized and reported in group form. Please do not include account numbers, passwords, bank credentials, or other sensitive financial identifiers in open-ended responses. Any signed consent form will be stored separately from questionnaire responses where practicable, and access to research records will be limited to the researchers and authorized academic evaluators.

**Questions**

If you have questions about the study or your participation, you may contact the researchers through the contact details provided by the research team.

**Consent Statement**

By signing below, I confirm that I have read and understood the information above, had the opportunity to ask questions, and voluntarily agree to participate in the research activities explained to me. I understand that I may withdraw at any time.

**APPENDIX C**

## **System Usability Scale (SUS) Questionnaire**

**Instructions**

Please try the SmartSpend application or use its Demo Mode for approximately 10 minutes before answering this questionnaire. After exploring the application, indicate how strongly you agree or disagree with each statement based on your experience. Answer all ten statements. Do not include the additional profile and comment questions when computing the SUS score.

**Response Scale**

1 – Strongly Disagree

2 – Disagree

3 – Neutral

4 – Agree

5 – Strongly Agree

**SUS Statements**

| No. | Statement | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | I think that I would like to use this system frequently. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ |
| 2 | I found the system unnecessarily complex. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ |
| 3 | I thought the system was easy to use. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ |
| 4 | I think that I would need the support of a technical person to be able to use this system. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ |
| 5 | I found the various functions in this system were well integrated. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ |
| 6 | I thought there was too much inconsistency in this system. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ |
| 7 | I would imagine that most people would learn to use this system very quickly. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ |
| 8 | I found the system very cumbersome / awkward to use. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ |
| 9 | I felt very confident using the system. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ |

**SUS Scoring Procedure (For Researchers)**

The SUS consists of ten items. For odd-numbered items (1, 3, 5, 7, and 9), subtract 1 from the respondent’s selected response. For even-numbered items (2, 4, 6, 8, and 10), subtract the selected response from 5\. Add the adjusted item scores and multiply the total by 2.5. The resulting SUS score ranges from 0 to 100\.

The study identifies a target SUS score of 80 or above as its acceptance threshold. Interpret the computed score using the interpretation approach described in Chapter II and the cited SUS literature. Do not calculate the SUS score using the additional profile or comment questions.

Note: The ten SUS statements above preserve the standard item wording and order. The supplementary profile questions are reported separately and are not part of the standardized SUS instrument.
